# Draft:Edwar J. Scully III

Edward J. Scully III
Edward Joseph Scully III (June 22, 1940 – December 24, 2018) was a lieutenant colonel in the United States Army, a Vietnam War veteran, a Special Forces officer, and a civilian aviation professional. He was inducted into the Delaware Aviation Hall of Fame in 2017.
Early life and education
Scully was born in Wilmington, Delaware, to Edward Joseph and Helen (Sabbata) Scully. He attended St. Ann School and graduated from Salesianum School in 1958.
Military career
Scully joined the United States Army in 1961 and served until 1988, retiring at the rank of lieutenant colonel. He served in the Vietnam War from June 1968 to December 1969 as a Special Forces "A" Team commander. Scully completed flight school and was qualified in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft. During his career, he held positions including Rotary Wing Commander at Davison Army Airfield D, Deputy Director for Aviation at the U.S. Army Training and Doctrine Command, and Deputy Inspector General of the U.S. Atlantic Command.
He received numerous military awards, including the Legion of Merit, Bronze Star for Valor, Bronze Star for Service, the Purple Heart, the Joint Service Meritorious Medal, the Meritorious Service Medal, and the Air Medal.
Later career
After retiring from the Army, Scully worked at Summit Aviation in Middletown, Delaware. He held management roles supporting aviation operations for military and government clients and contributed to programs including support for the Delaware State Police Aviation Branch. He retired from Summit Aviation in June 2013 after 25 years but continued to serve as a consultant.
Awards and recognition
Scully was inducted into the Delaware Aviation Hall of Fame in 2017 and the Salesianum School Hall of Fame in 2018. He also received the Bronze Honorable Order of St. Michael.
Death
Scully died on December 24, 2018, at Christiana Hospital in Wilmington, Delaware, at the age of 78. He is buried in Arlington National Cemetery.
